physical: A driven oscillator responds most strongly near its natural frequency; the width of that response grows with the damping, and the peak height falls with it (Q = ω0/Δω).
reflected_sentence: The reading turns around: a sharp response near a natural rate is easier with receptivity, where a drain had broadened it and lowered its peak.
rule_reason: One resistance-cost in the block, rising with the damping coefficient; odd count, so the reading turns around.
interpretation: One cost in the block turns the reading: harder becomes easier with receptivity. Frequency is not a rate, so it is not used for the width. Movement is the only frozen partner in the formula, and it does not name the width.
closing: One listed cost rises with the damping coefficient, an odd count, so the reading turns. Mass in the denominator was not added as a second cost. Physical frequency was not mapped to Frequency. No new word was introduced.
